bib.title: Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v3, 6 Jan 2016, journal-style extension of the NIPS 2015 paper [10])

read.skipped: Only detection-label clutter from Figures 5/6 and glyph codes of Figure 4 were skimmed; references skimmed for lineage.

question: Can region proposals be computed by a fully convolutional network that shares convolutional features with the detector, making proposals nearly free while keeping or improving detection accuracy?
hypothesis: Convolutional feature maps used by region-based detectors can also generate region proposals, so a learned RPN on shared features beats Selective Search in speed without losing accuracy.
contributions: Region Proposal Network (RPN): fully convolutional, predicts boxes and objectness at each position
Anchor boxes as a pyramid of regression references, translation invariant, single-scale images and filters
4-step alternating training to share conv layers between RPN and Fast R-CNN
5 fps (VGG-16) with state of the art mAP on VOC 2007/2012 and COCO with 300 proposals

method.summary: Faster R-CNN = RPN (3x3 conv, then sibling 1x1 cls and reg layers over k anchors per position) feeding a Fast R-CNN detector, with conv layers shared via 4-step alternating training. Evaluated with ZF and VGG-16 backbones on PASCAL VOC 2007/2012 and MS COCO, plus ablations on sharing, cls/reg, anchors and lambda.

datasets.name: PASCAL VOC 2007
datasets.size: about 5k trainval images and 5k test images, 20 categories
datasets.preprocessing: images rescaled so shorter side s = 600 px, single scale

datasets.name: PASCAL VOC 2012
datasets.split: 07++12 = VOC07 trainval+test and VOC12 trainval for training; VOC12 test for eval

datasets.name: MS COCO
datasets.split: train / trainval to train; val and test-dev to eval

models.name: Faster R-CNN with VGG-16
models.init_from: ImageNet-pretrained public VGG-16; conv3_1 and up tuned

training.objective: Eq. 1: L = (1/Ncls) sum Lcls(pi,pi*) + lambda (1/Nreg) sum pi* Lreg(ti,ti*); Lcls log loss over 2 classes (2-way softmax), Lreg smooth L1 on box params tx=(x-xa)/wa, ty=(y-ya)/ha, tw=log(w/wa), th=log(h/ha); Ncls=256, Nreg~2,400, lambda=10
training.lr: 0.001 for first 60k mini-batches then 0.0001 for next 20k (VOC); COCO: 0.003 for 240k then 0.0003 for 80k iterations
training.batch_size: RPN: 1 image per mini-batch with 256 sampled anchors, positive:negative up to 1:1 (pad with negatives if fewer than 128 positives); COCO 8-GPU: effective 8 for RPN (1 per GPU), 16 for Fast R-CNN (2 per GPU)
training.steps: VOC: 60k + 20k mini-batches; COCO: 240k + 80k iterations, for each of RPN step and Fast R-CNN step
training.regularisation: new layers init zero-mean Gaussian std 0.01; cross-boundary anchors ignored in training (about 6000 of about 20000 anchors remain for 1000x600 image)

other.anchor_labels: positive: highest IoU with a GT box, or IoU > 0.7 with any GT; negative: IoU < 0.3 for all GT; others ignored
other.nms: IoU 0.7 on cls scores, leaves about 2000 proposals; Fast R-CNN trained on 2000 RPN proposals, tested with top-N
other.four_step_alternating: 1 train RPN from ImageNet; 2 train separate Fast R-CNN on step-1 proposals; 3 init RPN from detector, fix shared conv, tune RPN-only layers; 4 fix shared conv, tune Fast R-CNN-only layers; more iterations gave negligible improvement
other.approximate_joint_training: reduces training time by about 25-50%, close results (no table)
other.coco_negatives: Fast R-CNN negatives defined as max IoU in [0, 0.5) instead of [0.1, 0.5)
other.voc_to_coco_finetune: COCO model replaces ImageNet init; softmax over 20 categories plus background

inference.decoding: RPN proposals, NMS at IoU 0.7, top-N (300 default) fed to Fast R-CNN
inference.samples: single run, single scale (s = 600), no seeds stated

parameters.cross_boundary_boxes: clipped to image boundary at test time

metrics.name: mAP (VOC)
metrics.definition: detection mean Average Precision on PASCAL VOC

metrics.name: mAP@0.5 and mAP@[.5,.95] (COCO)
metrics.definition: mAP averaged over IoU in [0.5:0.05:0.95], and at IoU 0.5

metrics.name: Timing
metrics.definition: ms per image on K40 GPU (SS on CPU), conv + proposal + region-wise

metrics.name: Recall vs IoU
metrics.definition: proposal recall at different IoU with GT, top-300/1000/2000 (Fig. 4)

eval.protocol: Single run per configuration; no seeds, variance or significance tests stated.

availability.data: public PASCAL VOC and MS COCO

limits: Single-scale input and stride 16 only; authors say smaller stride may improve accuracy
Anchor hyper-parameters 'not carefully chosen'; ablations only on VOC07 with VGG-16
All experiments use 4-step alternating training; approximate joint training claimed close but no numbers; exact joint training left out of scope
Speed comparison is GPU vs CPU for SS, which the authors call inequitable
Recall-vs-IoU only loosely tied to mAP
No seeds, variances or significance tests

terms.definition: reference boxes centered at the sliding window, each with a scale and aspect ratio; k=9 by default
Region Proposal Network: a fully convolutional network that takes an image of any size and outputs rectangular object proposals each with an objectness score
